unmapped_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 10 h gives a Vickers hardness of 961.1 ± 19.6 HV (Table 2), the second highest hardness among all 15Al aging conditions, just below the global 15Al maximum of 965.6 ± 7.6 HV obtained at 600 °C/6 h.

For the 15Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation at 550 °C is nearly complete after 6 h (Fig 4b), and by 10 h the SE-SEM structure is a uniform β-Mn matrix with fine new precipitates (Fig 7, 550 °C − 10 h panel).

The 15Al alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.85 g·cm^-3 (b0017); the reported ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g corresponds to the peak-hardness 15Al condition (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu), not explicitly to the 550 °C/10 h condition.

The 15Al alloy shows the fastest β-Mn precipitation kinetics: within 3 h of aging at 525 °C the α matrix was almost completely transformed into β-Mn, and at 550 °C this near-complete transformation occurred within about 6 h, versus 6 h (17Al) and 10 h (19Al) at 550 °C for the higher-Al alloys.

Reported nanoindentation hardness (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa) and intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.1 ± 0.3 GPa) for 15Al were measured on the hardest sample (600 °C/6 h, 965.6 HV), not on the 550 °C/10 h condition, so they are not assigned to this sample.
